neighbours.label: the verb (is/was/be) right after a cost/effort/amount/scale/losses noun OF something spelled out as vast ('the cost of rebuilding the entire network is'), setting up a word like 'enormous'; quiet when the measured thing is everyday-sized or the noun is not a measure (color, flavor)
neighbours.short: verb before 'enormous' after cost/scale of something vast
fire: The cost of rebuilding the entire national power grid is enormous.
Experts agree that the scale of the destruction across the whole continent was staggering.
The effort required to map every star in the galaxy would be immense.
The amount of water flowing through the Amazon basin each year is almost unimaginable.
Officials admitted that the losses of the global shipping industry during the crisis were colossal.
The price of relocating the country's entire capital city is astronomical.
Historians say the toll of the war on every nation in Europe was devastating.
The volume of data generated by all the world's sensors is vast.
quiet: The cost of replacing the kitchen faucet is about forty dollars.
The color of the entire national flag is a deep red.
The effort required to tie my shoelaces this morning was minimal.
The amount of sugar in this cup of tea is just one spoonful.
The flavor of the whole continent's cuisine is rich and varied.
The price of a single bus ticket is two euros.
The shape of the entire galaxy is a flattened spiral.
We rebuilt the entire network last year, and everyone was relieved.

predictions: blind test (label-only second author); expect most fire items above 0.20, near misses low; 'toll of the war' and 'Amazon basin' may be weaker
notes: Step-in reader of bonsai1/L25/N8045+ (drop 0.66). Feeders-first arm: top feeders L26/N1935- ('how' / 'some of' before a degree word) and L26/N1942- ('as' in 'as early as', 'no matter how') are degree-slot predictors; this pole narrows that to large magnitude. Solver: no leak; silent on gerund subjects without a measure noun ('Feeding every child ... was').
